stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 17%, and then the new price is decreased by 23%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 17% increase: $100 \times (1 + 17/100) = 117.00$. After a 23% decrease on 117.00: $117.00 \times (1 - 23/100) = 90.09$. Net change $= 90.09 - 100 = -9.91\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 17 - 23 - \dfrac{391}{100} = -9.91\%$.
